statement_id: CV-THM-SATURATION-INTRO / CV-SP-THM-ONE-COFACTOR with CV-SP-LEM-LINE-GCD (cp03 introduction.tex l.40; presentations.tex l.753)
who: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, AG_POLISH cluster reader (follow-up 25 Nov)
outcome: key step confirmed: (f_i)=g(h_i) and (f):m^infty=(g) iff V(h_1..h_s) is empty, so on any line of the chart x_0=1 the cofactor restrictions are coprime and gcd(f_i|line)=g|line up to a unit; reducing the other f_i modulo the low-degree f_j|line by modular exponentiation keeps binary degrees affordable; H_j values come out up to the constant fixed by the base point a. Interpolation and the translated Hasse extraction read, not re-derived

who: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, AG_POLISH cluster reader (follow-up 25 Nov)
outcome: own program agpolish/cv_onecof.py over F_5: g=y^2z-x^3-xz^2, cofactors h1=2x+3y+z, h2 of degree 25, h3 of degree 40 (no common zero); univariate gcds with modular exponentiation return h1(z)/h1(a) correctly at every point of F_5^3 off the line through 0 and a (the 4 exceptions lie on that line, where the homogeneous cofactors share the zero 0; the paper's chart x_0=1 excludes them); g recovered exactly; h_5(g)=2 and #X(F_5)=4≡1-2

statement_id: CV-THM-SATURATION-CI-INTRO (cp03 introduction.tex l.50; saturation_ci.tex), background formula
who: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, AG_POLISH cluster reader (follow-up 25 Nov)
outcome: own program agpolish/cv_ci.py: for the smooth quadric-intersection curve q1=sum x_i^2, q2=x^2+2y^2+3z^2+4w^2 over F_5, the Koszul coefficient [(xyzw)^4](q1q2)^4 = 3 and #X(F_5)=8≡1-3; the coefficient is unchanged under three changes of regular generators (det 1,1,2). This checks the coefficient formula the theorem rests on, not its annihilator/finite-extension/norm-descent step, which was not checked
